verdict: 2026-08-03 06:08:05 PM PDT — Not sound yet. Vendoring the adapter, using Fireworks `json_schema`, validating again with `jsonschema`, and centralizing model routes are good choices. However, the proposed shape stops short of the executable harness this second backend was supposed to force, does not define sufficient pass-specific context for a non-agentic reviewer, and leaves the Python runtime unversioned.

findings.title: The executable seam stops at the API adapter
findings.locus: Design sketch — Skill dispatch and Testing; AC-5 and AC-7 falsification plans
findings.claim: Backend orchestration—pass selection, context assembly, correctness fan-out, joining, and artifact promotion—remains copied imperative prose across `frame/SKILL.md` and `review/SKILL.md`. This is the heavy seam that the existing test charter explicitly said the second backend would force. Consequently, AC-5 and AC-7 rely on implementation-token drift pins such as PID capture and stop wording rather than behavioral oracles. The proposed adapter suite is also absent from the stated gate, `.claude/workflow.json` test command, and CI gate command, so its real oracles would not run. The AC-7 `reviewer` oracle for detecting different sibling payloads is blind to—and effectively circular with—the context discrepancy it is meant to catch.
findings.alternative: Make one executable Fireworks runner the backend boundary. Give it a declarative pass table mapping design, approach, correctness, and hidden-failure to prompt, schema, required context, output, and critic grouping. Let it own concurrent execution and all-or-nothing promotion; leave each skill with a thin invocation. Exercise that runner behaviorally and add its suite to the configured and CI gates.
findings.win: Removes repeated command-block logic, centralizes the fail-closed invariant, and turns AC-5 through AC-7 from prose-token checks into executable behavior with meaningful failure signals.

findings.title: The pushed-context contract cannot preserve reviewer grounding
findings.locus: AC-6, its falsification plan, and Design sketch — Adapter / Size guard
findings.claim: The plan treats `AGENTS.md`, story, and non-empty diff as the generic required inputs, but the four invocations have different grounding. Frame design runs before a diff exists and requires surrounding code plus dependency manifests; approach requires the full changed files and dependency manifest, not merely their diff; correctness requires the story, diff, and relevant history. These product surfaces are not enumerated, so a schema-valid but blind review can pass. The byte approximation also does not establish fail-closed behavior: Fireworks exposes `context_length_exceeded_behavior` with truncating behavior unless error semantics are requested, while `--check-models` only verifies route existence rather than comparing the stored context length with live metadata. See the [Fireworks Chat Completions API](https://docs.fireworks.ai/api-reference/post-chatcompletions).
findings.alternative: Define a declarative context profile per pass. Design should require the story, contract, manifests, and an explicit list of surrounding files selected during framing; approach should add diff, log, manifests, and full contents of every changed file; correctness should carry its own enumerated bundle. Set provider overflow behavior to `error`, reserve an explicit output-token budget, fail on `finish_reason: length`, and have `--check-models` compare stored and live context lengths. Falsify each pass profile independently.
findings.win: Eliminates the impossible frame-time non-empty-diff requirement and prevents incomplete or silently truncated context from producing a false-clean review.

findings.title: The runtime dependency contract is outside the repository
findings.locus: Open question Q3; Design sketch — Shape / Validation
findings.claim: The repository has no Python dependency manifest, yet the proposed source of truth consists only of a module and routing JSON while requiring `openai` and `jsonschema`. Q3 recommends a manually created user-local virtualenv without specifying a versioned dependency contract or stable interpreter entrypoint. Failing safely when imports are absent proves only the error path; it does not make the installed backend reproducible. The AC-1 `/opt` row is also an implementation-shaped legacy surface: if direct invocation of the installed copy is chosen, the actual product surfaces are the installed entrypoint and its runtime environment, while `/opt` should be explicitly excluded.
findings.alternative: Resolve Q3 before approval and add a small versioned dependency manifest—such as a dedicated `requirements` file or `pyproject.toml` with bounded versions—plus one deterministic user-local entrypoint/bootstrap command. `install.sh` may remain an offline file copier, but deployment checks should verify the entrypoint and environment separately. Update AC-8's enumerated scope accordingly.
findings.win: Makes the reviewed repository authoritative for both code and runtime requirements, removes dependence on the admin-owned `/opt` environment, and allows clean-environment tests to reproduce successful execution rather than only missing-dependency failure.
